chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who prayed but did not know whether he prayed two, three, or four [rak'at], he (peace be upon him) said: 'He stands and prays two [rak'at] while standing, then offers the salām, then he prays two [rak'at] while sitting, and offers the salām. So if it was four [rak'at], the two [rak'at] are optional (nafl), otherwise the four are complete.'

key_terms.يُسَلِّمُ: Offers the salām (greeting of peace concluding the prayer)

ai.seo_question: What is the procedure for correcting prayer when one is unsure if they prayed two, three, or four rak'at?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi outlines the Shia jurisprudence for 'shakk al-thalathah' (doubt between two, three, and four rak'at), prescribing a method of building upon the lower number (iqti'a) by adding two standing and two sitting rak'at. This approach ensures the validity of the prayer regardless of whether the actual count was three or four, reflecting the principle of certainty being overridden by probable doubt. It highlights the practical application of 'istishab' (presumption of continuity) in daily worship, distinguishing Shia fiqh from other schools on handling specific numerical ambiguities.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from one of his companions,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws regarding a man who prays but he does not know whether he has prayed two or three or four. Heasws said: ‘He should stand and pray two Rak’at from a standing, then offer Salām, then he should pray two Rak’at from sitting and she should offer Salām. So if it was so that (he had prayed) four Rak’at, the two Rak’at would be (counted as) optional, or else the four would be complete’.
en.sarwar: 6. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from certain persons of his people who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abdullah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam,

about the case of one who performs Salah (prayer) and doubts if he has performed two or four Rak’ah, has said, ‘ He stands up and performs two Rak’ah in a standing position. He then says the phrase of offering greeting of peace, then performs two Rak’ah in a sitting position, and says the phrase of offering greeting of peace. If, in fact, they were four Rak’ah the two Rak’ah become optional; otherwise, they complete the four Rak’ah.’”
